prompt:
A high oblique SUBMERSIBLE establishing shot of a lavishly decorated haunted sunken sea-palace at surface-light, portrait 9:16. The camera floats about 40 meters ABOVE the courtyard and well BACK from the foreground pavilion, around the height of the main coral-spire's upper half. It looks diagonally DOWN across the sea-palace at roughly 20–25 degrees below horizontal with a wide 24 mm lens. A turquoise-lit rippling surface, surface glow at left and distant murky reef horizon remain clearly visible in the upper third. The composition must immediately read as a gliding submersible looking down into a sunken palace compound.

Show broad TOP SURFACES of both long side-colonnade roofs and the small central pavilion roof. See DOWN into the rectangular sunken pool, over its near parapet, with paving and steps receding away below the camera. People are tiny figures seen from above. The front boundary occupies a narrow foreground strip. The complete tall coral-spire stands in the background, with water around its finials. The small four-column Ganesha pavilion is well below the camera, its roof about one quarter of frame width, with open courtyard separating it from the tower. Its roof partly occludes the tiny seated idol. This is a grand view of the whole courtyard, not a close shrine portrait. Keep the surface and horizon while retaining clear downward perspective; neither an eye-level facade view nor a vertical overhead map.

Blue-black intricately eroded basalt, one nine-tier coral spire, one small square four-column pavilion with a ribbed coral cap, ribbed coral beam and three steps. All pavilion sides are open, including the rear. A tiny teal-ivory, gold-crowned Ganesha occupies its flower-covered pedestal between two lamps; facial details are not resolved from this height. No closed inner sanctuary or back wall.

Lavish wedding decoration is distributed across the entire aerial view: three broad tiers of crimson-ivory-teal floral swags on the tower, layered garlands and kelp fronds along BOTH colonnades, floral trim on the pavilion's outer beam and columns, white kolam and flower rangoli in the side courtyards, rows of shell lanterns, petal borders along steps and tank edges, and anchored shell bowls in the pool. These details stay small in the landscape; never lower or move the camera closer to show them. The central forward-down flight route remains clear. Cold surface-light, long shadows, subtle reflections, submerged depth and premium dimensional storybook illustration. No text, watermark or additional shrine.
